exposure: Type of anaesthesia for caesarean section (general vs. regional)
intubation for caesarean section with suxamethonium
Type of neuromuscular blocking agent for intubation (rocuronium vs. suxamethonium)
intubation for caesarean section with rocuronium
Type of caesarean section (elective vs. emergency)
outcome: Neonatal Apgar score at 1, 5, and 10 minutes
cohort: 10,226 newborns delivered by 10,119 women in the Czech Republic and Slovakia
finding: Among out-of-risk newborns (term, birth weight >= 2500g, elective caesarean section), there was no difference in Apgar scores between general and regional anaesthesia for caesarean section.
mod_finding: The study found no difference in neonatal outcomes (Apgar scores) between cesarean deliveries performed under general anesthesia compared to regional anesthesia in out-of-risk newborns.
